spec.purpose: Track the fifty outcomes required to turn the public configuration catalog into a useful path from Helm, AICR, cub installer, OCI, or Kubernetes YAML through ConfigHub and back to deployable OCI.

statusDefinitions.available: The named scope has a usable path, committed evidence, and a verifier. This does not imply support for every chart, source, or target.
statusDefinitions.blocked: A named defect or external decision currently prevents the completion check from passing.
statusDefinitions.partial: A representative path works, but an important delivery target, source type, catalog segment, lifecycle case, or product surface remains open.
statusDefinitions.planned: The outcome is agreed but does not yet have an end-to-end proof.

tasks.name: Pull one ready-made OCI package without an account
tasks.next: Keep every published package reference current when recipes or package contents change.
tasks.outcome: A new user can pull a public catalog package by immutable digest without ConfigHub or registry credentials.

tasks.name: Explain the package source and provenance
tasks.next: Keep the source record beside every additional format added to the catalog.
tasks.outcome: A user can identify the chart, version, preset config, source lock, and package digest before deployment.

tasks.name: Inspect recorded Helm inputs and rendered objects
tasks.next: Extend the same readable input record to every non-Helm source format.
tasks.outcome: A user can read the values, namespace, release name, capabilities, source lock, and exact Kubernetes objects.

tasks.name: Verify Helm-equivalent output
tasks.next: Rerun parity whenever a chart version, preset config, renderer, or target capability profile changes.
tasks.outcome: The recorded chart, inputs, and target capabilities reproduce the same semantic Kubernetes objects as Helm.

tasks.name: Show prerequisites and lifecycle work before deployment
tasks.next: Turn more candidate routes into chart-specific receipts and keep unsupported routes as named blockers.
tasks.outcome: Secrets, CRDs, hooks, setup jobs, target facts, and their execution route are visible beside the rendered objects.

tasks.name: Run the public path locally without ConfigHub
tasks.next: Keep the command surface aligned with released cub installer behavior.
tasks.outcome: A user can render and inspect a package locally with no ConfigHub server, account, or Kubernetes cluster.

tasks.name: Run the anonymous path in CI
tasks.next: Publish a copyable CI workflow for each supported input family.
tasks.outcome: CI can pull, render, package, and compare public configuration without ConfigHub credentials.

tasks.name: Offer a hosted anonymous inspection service
tasks.next: Choose the hosting and abuse-control model, then prove one public request from source to immutable OCI.
tasks.outcome: A user can submit or select public source material, inspect the result, and obtain OCI without signing in.

tasks.name: Review a chart and values supplied by the user
tasks.next: Add private-chart and dependency-auth examples without weakening source-lock requirements.
tasks.outcome: A user can render a chart and values from their team, inspect exact objects, and compare the result with defaults.

tasks.name: Review values proposed by AI
tasks.next: Add more chart classes and target-aware checks rather than treating one NGINX example as universal.
tasks.outcome: An AI-proposed values file becomes an exact object diff with checks and a corrected reviewed result.

tasks.name: Build deployable OCI from reviewed source
tasks.next: Generalize the build entry point across Helm, AICR, installer packages, and plain Kubernetes YAML.
tasks.outcome: Reviewed source configuration can be packaged as literal OCI and pulled back to the same object set.

tasks.name: Inspect and test an existing OCI package
tasks.next: Add signature checks and consumer-specific validation without confusing them with the package inspection report.
tasks.outcome: A user can start with OCI, inspect its Kubernetes objects and companion records, and run checks without claiming it in ConfigHub.

tasks.name: Transform OCI to OCI without requiring ConfigHub
tasks.next: Release cub with the merged companion-record import fix, then add patch-file input and signature checks. The worked NGINX output already has an authenticated publication receipt and anonymous pull-back check.
tasks.outcome: An existing OCI can be checked or changed and emitted as a new immutable OCI while preserving source records.

tasks.name: Turn AICR input into managed configuration
tasks.next: Deliver the promoted configuration through Argo CD and Flux and record live GPU-target evidence.
tasks.outcome: One AICR bundle is generated, reviewed, published as OCI, uploaded as a base variant, and promoted to development and staging.

tasks.name: Turn a cub installer package into rendered OCI
tasks.next: Keep both the multi-preset source packages and the rendered OCI output path synchronized with current installer behavior.
tasks.outcome: A user can pull a multi-preset installer package, select one base, render its exact Kubernetes objects, and write and verify those objects as a separate OCI artifact.

tasks.name: Upload literal Kubernetes YAML without rerendering
tasks.next: Continue the same four-object base through a derived variant and release only when that adds a lesson not already covered by the main ConfigHub tutorial.
tasks.outcome: Existing Kubernetes YAML can become ConfigHub Units while preserving the reviewed object set.

tasks.name: Claim reviewed OCI as a ConfigHub base variant
tasks.next: Use one upload contract for all supported source-neutral OCI inputs.
tasks.outcome: A reviewed OCI can become a named ConfigHub Space and base variant with exact Units and source context.

tasks.name: Attach render context and route intent to every base variant
tasks.next: Work through the generated route and target-prerequisite gaps until every base has an exact attached contract or an explicit no-extra-work decision.
tasks.outcome: Each base records source inputs, render context, produced objects, prerequisites, and lifecycle routes.

tasks.name: Create derived variants by editing exact objects
tasks.next: Keep derived changes linked to their base and add target-bound receipts where delivery is claimed.
tasks.outcome: A team can clone a reviewed base, change exact Kubernetes fields without rerendering Helm, and inspect the resulting diff.

tasks.name: Keep approved object edits through source upgrades
tasks.next: Repeat the upgrade proof on another chart and add a useful mutation preview for promotion dry runs.
tasks.outcome: A source upgrade can rebuild the base while reapplying reviewed post-render changes and surfacing conflicts.

tasks.name: Promote through development staging and production
tasks.next: Add the ordinary product interface and repeat destination preflight, rollback, and live comparison across more chart and target classes.
tasks.outcome: A reviewed revision can move through named environments in order with exact diffs and environment-specific policy.

tasks.name: Block unsafe configuration and require approval at high-risk boundaries
tasks.next: Add resource-aware field checks for more custom-resource APIs without weakening the common policy or making ordinary warnings blocking.
tasks.outcome: Every policy-covered Space receives the eight common checks. Production releases and system configuration also require approval, while ordinary development and staging workloads do not.

tasks.name: Make policy checks source-neutral
tasks.next: Add checks for more custom-resource versions and teach target-specific checks to read recorded target facts instead of hard-coding one cluster's limits.
tasks.outcome: One policy profile applies shared checks to Helm, AICR, installer, Kubara, Sveltos, and literal Kubernetes data, limits ordinary workload checks to known Kubernetes kinds, and uses AICR checks for its deeper fields.

tasks.name: Publish reviewed ConfigHub Units as OCI
tasks.next: Keep the release and portable OCI roles clearly distinguished in every guide and command.
tasks.outcome: ConfigHub can publish the exact reviewed Units as immutable OCI for an external delivery controller.

tasks.name: Preserve digest identity and provenance through the round trip
tasks.next: Deliver and observe the AICR path on a suitable GPU target; it is the one source family whose standardized chain still stops at the output OCI.
tasks.outcome: Input digest, ConfigHub revision, output digest, delivery result, and observation can be followed as one evidence chain.

tasks.name: Deliver reviewed OCI through Argo CD
tasks.next: Maintain fresh controller and workload receipts for every path that claims Argo CD delivery.
tasks.outcome: Selected reviewed ConfigHub configurations are pulled by Argo CD and converge to the expected Kubernetes objects.

tasks.name: Deliver reviewed OCI through Flux
tasks.next: Maintain the ConfigHub-output Flux receipt and add representative AICR and lifecycle-route Flux evidence.
tasks.outcome: Flux can consume the reviewed literal OCI without rerendering the source and produce observed workload evidence.

tasks.name: Deliver reviewed objects by direct apply
tasks.next: Keep direct apply as a simple option while making interruptions and lifecycle ordering explicit.
tasks.outcome: A user can inspect generated files and apply the same reviewed object set directly to Kubernetes.

tasks.name: Record live convergence and observation freshness
tasks.next: Store more live observations in ConfigHub and refresh receipts when target state or packages change.
tasks.outcome: Delivery claims include controller status, object equality, workload health, observer identity, and observation time.

tasks.name: Roll back or unwind a reviewed change
tasks.next: Repeat the receipt pattern for charts with CRD changes, hooks, or data migrations whose rollback limits need a chart-specific recovery plan.
tasks.outcome: A team can identify the prior revision, restore reversible fields, and retain an operation record without hiding irreversible migrations.

tasks.name: Preview fleet blast radius before rollout
tasks.next: Increase measured cases and report misses and false predictions for every supported inheritance pattern.
tasks.outcome: A candidate change names the variants, targets, objects, and fields expected to change before promotion.

tasks.name: Roll out one revision in bounded waves
tasks.next: Prove the same bounded rollout using a mixed-source platform fleet and production approval.
tasks.outcome: One reviewed OCI digest can move from a pilot target to a larger target set with per-wave checks and observations.

tasks.name: Manage a Sveltos fleet from reviewed OCI
tasks.next: Add rollback, larger selectors, and a source update that exercises ConfigHub variant propagation.
tasks.outcome: ConfigHub approves two OCI revisions and Sveltos expands Kyverno from a pilot cluster to a second cluster with drift recovery.

tasks.name: Manage a Kubara platform configuration
tasks.next: Add a multi-cluster Kubara rollout and show which fleet CRD fields are intended to vary.
tasks.outcome: One reviewed Kubara platform configuration is packaged, routed, delivered through Argo CD, and observed on a downstream application.

tasks.name: Distinguish workloads services and system configuration
tasks.next: Classify more catalog records only after their owner, target scope, gate set, rollout choice, and evidence are known.
tasks.outcome: Delivery policy and ownership can differ for user workloads, shared services, and cluster system configuration.

tasks.name: Complete the Upgrade App
tasks.next: Add the product App interface, automatic route selection, persistent history, and a lifecycle-aware rollback path.
tasks.outcome: The App previews impact, tests a candidate, preserves approved edits, promotes it, and checks the rollout.

tasks.name: Complete the Hooks and CRDs App
tasks.next: Add the product App interface and automatic route selection, then test rollback and post-success cleanup before widening the claim.
tasks.outcome: The App checks prerequisites, runs chart-specific setup in the recorded order, and stores receipts for each delivery method.

tasks.name: Complete the RBAC Review App
tasks.next: Query a real fleet binding graph and prove Flux delivery, rollback, and rollout of an approved correction.
tasks.outcome: The App finds broad permissions, proposes an exact correction, requires approval, publishes OCI, and checks the live result.

tasks.name: Complete the Fleet Platform App
tasks.next: Run one mixed-source fleet wave through a shared interface with target-level observations.
tasks.outcome: The App assigns Helm, AICR, Kubara, or Sveltos-derived platform configuration to cluster groups and manages rollout waves.

tasks.name: Complete the AI Change Review App
tasks.next: Add AICR-aware policy, Kubernetes delivery, promotion, rollback, and live workload evidence.
tasks.outcome: The App turns an agent proposal into exact objects, diffs, checks, approval, delivery, observation, and unwind.

tasks.name: Maintain public packages for the top 100 Helm charts
tasks.next: Keep all packages reproducible and remove any public reference that no longer passes its package verifier.
tasks.outcome: One hundred chart entries have recipe and package proof artifacts plus public OCI references.

tasks.name: Complete production-scoped support decisions for the top 20
tasks.next: Keep supported decisions tied to fresh target and image evidence, and require a new hardened base before reopening a rejected or superseded scope.
tasks.outcome: Each top-20 chart states its supported target scope, required prerequisites, scans, lifecycle work, live evidence, and remaining limits.

tasks.name: Promote the next 80 from proof-grade to useful catalog configs
tasks.next: Build the remaining useful-base proposals and review promotion candidates in evidence order.
tasks.outcome: More charts gain reviewed starting presets, useful variants, target guidance, and selected live evidence rather than default-only proof.

tasks.name: Expand the catalog beyond Helm
tasks.next: Add stable browse pages and ready-to-use artifacts for every source family rather than leaving them only in demonstrations.
tasks.outcome: The catalog explains and proves AICR, cub installer, literal OCI, Kubara, Sveltos, and Kubernetes YAML alongside Helm.

tasks.name: Let users browse by starting point and next job
tasks.next: Keep both navigation tables and their linked source pages current as starting points and jobs change.
tasks.outcome: A user can enter by Helm, AICR, installer, OCI, or YAML and then choose inspect, install, upload, customize, promote, deliver, operate, or build an App.

tasks.name: Put one plain-English README in every live demo Space
tasks.next: Keep README Units synchronized whenever a Space, preset config, route, or linked chart page changes.
tasks.outcome: A visitor opening a helm-catalog Space can understand why it exists, what it contains, how it was made, and where to find deeper evidence.

tasks.name: Join chart pages to packages scripts README and proof
tasks.next: Keep generated links valid and preserve plain-English summaries as the catalog gains more source formats.
tasks.outcome: Every runnable preset card links to its public OCI, scripts, Hub README material, render record, rendered YAML, and relevant evidence.

tasks.name: Make hooks CRDs and setup work manageable per chart
tasks.next: Repeat destination-bound lifecycle promotion for more high-value route work orders and keep untested controller paths named.
tasks.outcome: Most real chart lifecycle cases use maintained chart-specific presets and routes, with tests and receipts rather than a universal replacement claim.

tasks.name: Keep the complete repository verification gate green
tasks.next: Rerun the complete gate whenever packages, receipts, generated data, docs, or public claims change.
tasks.outcome: Focused and broad verification agree that generated data, docs, packages, receipts, and public claims are current.

tasks.name: Measure whether new users understand and complete the journey
tasks.next: Run the six technically proved journeys with outside users and turn observed failures into tracked product, CLI, or content fixes.
tasks.outcome: Outside users can find a starting point, inspect or bring configuration, produce one deployable result, and understand why they would claim it in ConfigHub.
